title: Khun Borom and the Great Gourd
credit: From the old Lao story of Khun Borom, and of Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu, the grandfather and grandmother who are honoured every Lao New Year in Luang Prabang. Retold in our own words.

lines.text: Long, long ago, the land was quiet. There were no villages, no songs and no children.
say: Long, long ago, the land was quiet. There were no villages, no songs and no children.

lines.text: Only two old people lived there, with their little lion. Their names were Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu.
say: Only two old people lived there, with their little lion. Their names were Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer.

lines.text: High above, the Sky King looked down. "The land is too quiet," he said.
say: High above, the Sky King looked down.

lines.text: So he sent a gift down from the clouds: a big, strong buffalo.
say: So he sent a gift down from the clouds: a big, strong buffalo.

lines.text: With the buffalo, Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu made the first rice field. "Thank you, Sky King!" they called.
say: With the buffalo, Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer made the first rice field.

lines.text: The buffalo worked hard for many years. Then he was old and tired.
say: The buffalo worked hard for many years. Then he was old and tired.

lines.text: One evening he lay down in the soft grass for his last, long sleep. "Goodbye, old friend," said Pu Nyeu.
say: One evening he lay down in the soft grass for his last, long sleep.

lines.text: But where the buffalo slept, a little green vine began to grow.
say: But where the buffalo slept, a little green vine began to grow.

lines.text: On the vine grew a gourd. It grew big. Then bigger. Then bigger than a house!
say: On the vine grew a gourd. It grew big. Then bigger. Then bigger than a house!

lines.text: "What a gourd!" said Nya Nyeu. Little Lion sniffed it. Sniff, sniff!
say: said Ñah Ñer. Little Lion sniffed it. Sniff, sniff!

lines.text: One morning, the gourd went knock, knock, knock!
say: One morning, the gourd went knock, knock, knock!

lines.text: Pu Nyeu put his ear on the gourd. Inside, somebody laughed.
say: Poo Ñer put his ear on the gourd. Inside, somebody laughed.

lines.text: Somebody sang a song. A baby cried. A rooster crowed!
say: Somebody sang a song. A baby cried. A rooster crowed!

lines.text: "Who is in there?" asked Little Lion.
"It is dark in there," said Nya Nyeu. "Let's make a door."
Pu Nyeu made an iron stick hot in the fire. Sssss! He made two little holes in the gourd.
say: Poo Ñer made an iron stick hot in the fire. Sssss! He made two little holes in the gourd.

lines.text: Nya Nyeu cut the holes wider with her chisel. Tap, tap, tap! One was a round door. One was a square door.
say: Ñah Ñer cut the holes wider with her chisel. Tap, tap, tap! One was a round door. One was a square door.

lines.text: Then both doors opened, and out came people! One, two, three... more and more people!
say: Then both doors opened, and out came people! One, two, three... more and more people!

lines.text: After them came pigs and chickens, ducks and dogs, and a little buffalo!
say: After them came pigs and chickens, ducks and dogs, and a little buffalo!

lines.text: For three days and three nights, they came out of the great gourd. "Welcome to the sun, children!" said Nya Nyeu.
say: For three days and three nights, they came out of the great gourd.

lines.text: Soon there were people everywhere. The quiet land was full of houses, songs and children.
say: Soon there were people everywhere. The quiet land was full of houses, songs and children.

lines.text: But they did not share. "This is OUR mango tree!" "No! It is OUR mango tree!"
say: No! It is our mango tree!

lines.text: "We came out of the round door. We are the best!" "No! We came out of the square door. WE are the best!"
say: We came out of the round door. We are the best!
No! We came out of the square door. We are the best!

lines.text: They shouted all day long. Little Lion put his paws over his ears.
say: They shouted all day long. Little Lion put his paws over his ears.

lines.text: Pu Nyeu looked up at the sky. "Sky King," he called, "please help us!"
say: Poo Ñer looked up at the sky.

lines.text: The Sky King heard. He sent his own son, Khun Borom, to help.
say: The Sky King heard. He sent his own son, Koon Baw-lom, to help.

lines.text: Down from the sky came Khun Borom, riding a great white elephant.
say: Down from the sky came Koon Baw-lom, riding a great white elephant.

lines.text: Khun Borom was wise and kind. He showed the people how to grow rice, build houses and weave cloth.
say: Koon Baw-lom was wise and kind. He showed the people how to grow rice, build houses and weave cloth.

lines.text: "Remember," said Khun Borom. "Round door, square door: you all came from one gourd. You are one family."
say: Round door, square door: you all came from one gourd. You are one family.

lines.text: The people nodded. But the round-door people still sat on one side. The square-door people sat on the other.
say: The people nodded. But the round-door people still sat on one side. The square-door people sat on the other.

lines.text: All this time, the gourd's vine went on growing. Up and up it went, all the way to the sky.
say: All this time, the gourd's vine went on growing. Up and up it went, all the way to the sky.

lines.text: Its big leaves covered the sun. The land was dark and cold, and the rice stopped growing.
say: Its big leaves covered the sun. The land was dark and cold, and the rice stopped growing.

lines.text: "I can't see!" "I'm cold!" People bumped into each other in the dark.
say: People bumped into each other in the dark.

lines.text: Khun Borom lit a big fire. "Come close, everyone," he said.
say: Koon Baw-lom lit a big fire.

lines.text: They held hands so they would not fall. Nobody asked, "Which door are you from?"
say: They held hands so they would not fall. Nobody asked, Which door are you from?

lines.text: "I don't like the dark," said Little Lion. Nya Nyeu held him close.
say: said Little Lion. Ñah Ñer held him close.

lines.text: "We must cut the vine," said Khun Borom. "Who will do it?"
The vine was as tall as the sky. The strong men looked down at their feet. Nobody said a word.
say: The vine was as tall as the sky. The strong men looked down at their feet. Nobody said a word.

lines.text: Then two old voices said, "We will." It was Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu.
say: It was Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer.

lines.text: "But you are so old!" said the people. "Yes," said Nya Nyeu. "We have seen the sun many, many times. The children must see it too."
say: We have seen the sun many, many times. The children must see it too.

lines.text: "We ask for only one thing," said Pu Nyeu. "Remember us. When you sit down to eat, call our names."
say: We ask for only one thing,
Remember us. When you sit down to eat, call our names.

lines.text: "Will you come back?" asked Little Lion. "Every New Year," said Nya Nyeu. "That is a promise. Listen for the drums."
say: That is a promise. Listen for the drums.

lines.text: Chop, chop, chop! Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu cut the great vine, day after day.
say: Chop, chop, chop! Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer cut the great vine, day after day.

lines.text: Everybody helped. Some brought water. Some brought rice. Even Khun Borom carried water.
say: Everybody helped. Some brought water. Some brought rice. Even Koon Baw-lom carried water.

lines.text: For three long months they worked side by side, like one family. Nobody talked about doors any more.
say: For three long months they worked side by side, like one family. Nobody talked about doors any more.

lines.text: "Now stand back, children," said Pu Nyeu. "The last cut is ours."
CRACK! The great vine fell. The dark was gone. The sun came back!
say: Crack! The great vine fell. The dark was gone. The sun came back!

lines.text: The land was warm again. But where were Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu?
say: The land was warm again. But where were Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer?

lines.text: They were gone. They gave their lives to bring back the sun.
say: They were gone. They gave their lives to bring back the sun.

lines.text: "We will always remember them," said Khun Borom. "Now they keep our land safe."
say: Now they keep our land safe.

lines.text: That night, everybody ate together, one big family. Little Lion called first: "Come and eat, Pu Nyeu! Come and eat, Nya Nyeu!"
say: That night, everybody ate together, one big family. Little Lion called first:
Come and eat, Poo Ñer! Come and eat, Ñah Ñer!

lines.text: Today, many years later, people still remember. Every Lao New Year, the drums go boom, boom, boom!
say: Today, many years later, people still remember. Every Lao New Year, the drums go boom, boom, boom!

lines.text: Out come Pu Nyeu and Nya Nyeu to dance! They have big red faces and long, long hair. Little Lion dances too. They keep their promise every year.
say: Out come Poo Ñer and Ñah Ñer to dance! They have big red faces and long, long hair. Little Lion dances too. They keep their promise every year.

moral.text: We are one family. Round door, square door: everyone came from one gourd.
say: We are one family. Round door, square door: everyone came from one gourd.

moral.text: Old can be brave. The strong men were afraid. Two grandparents were not.
say: Old can be brave. The strong men were afraid. Two grandparents were not.

moral.text: Remember the people who help you. Say their names. Every Lao New Year, people still do.
say: Remember the people who help you. Say their names. Every Lao New Year, people still do.

moral.text: Word corner: two Lao words. Pu means grandfather. Nya means grandmother.
say: Word corner: two Lao words. Poo means grandfather. Ñah means grandmother.

game.text: Tap the wet mud to plant the rice. Count with me!
say: Tap the wet mud to plant the rice. Count with me!

game.text: Little Lion wants to see the top! Tap the glowing leaf.
say: Little Lion wants to see the top! Tap the glowing leaf.

game.text: Up, up, up! What a big gourd!
say: Up, up, up! What a big gourd!

game.text: Tap the gourd where it glows, and listen!
say: Tap the gourd where it glows, and listen!

game.text: So many voices! Somebody is in there!
say: So many voices! Somebody is in there!

game.text: Who wants to come out? Tap them and count with me!
say: Who wants to come out? Tap them and count with me!

game.text: It is too loud! Tap the shouting people so they stop and listen.
say: It is too loud! Tap the shouting people so they stop and listen.

game.text: Tap a thing, then tap where it goes!
say: Tap a thing, then tap where it goes!

game.text: Who is still out in the dark? Tap the shining eyes!
say: Who is still out in the dark? Tap the shining eyes!

game.text: Help them get ready! Find the axe, the rope, the water jar, the rice basket and the lamp.
say: Help them get ready! Find the axe, the rope, the water jar, the rice basket and the lamp.

game.text: The axe, to cut the vine!
say: The axe, to cut the vine!

game.text: The rope, to pull it down!
say: The rope, to pull it down!

game.text: The water jar, so they can drink!
say: The water jar, so they can drink!

game.text: The rice basket, so they can eat!
say: The rice basket, so they can eat!

game.text: The lamp, to see in the dark!
say: The lamp, to see in the dark!

game.text: Chop with them! Tap when the ring closes on the axe.
say: Chop with them! Tap when the ring closes on the axe.

game.text: Play the drums to call them! Listen, then tap the same.
say: Play the drums to call them! Listen, then tap the same.

game.text: Happy New Year! Here they are!
say: Happy New Year! Here they are!

punyeu: I am Pu Nyeu. Pu means grandfather.
My head cloth is red and white.
I tie a cloth round my waist.
nyanyeu: I am Nya Nyeu. Nya means grandmother.
A white flower is in my hair.
I tie my hair in a bun.
My sinh has a woven hem.
My skirt is called a sinh.
My shoulder cloth is called a pha biang.
lion: My mane is made of curls.
I have a round gold tag.
My tail has a gold tuft.
khunborom: I am Khun Borom. I came to help.
I wear a small gold crown.
My long cloth is red and gold.
I teach people to grow rice.
skyking: I can see the land below.
I sit on a soft cloud.
punyeu_dance: I am Pu Nyeu. I came back!
I have a big red face.
My hair is long and shaggy.
I come every Lao New Year.
nyanyeu_dance: I am Nya Nyeu. I came back!
My face is big and red.
I love the sound of drums.
I keep my promise every year.
turtle: A turtle can hide in its shell.
duck: A duck has a flat beak.
squirrel: A squirrel has a fluffy tail.
house: A house on stilts. Stilts are posts.
A water jar. It holds water.
fire: A clay pot sits by the fire.
plough: A plough. It makes the soil soft.
A plough is made of wood.
taro: A taro leaf. Big as an ear.
A taro leaf is big and green.
Rain rolls off a taro leaf.
mango-tree: A mango tree. Mangoes are sweet.
termite-mound: A termite mound. Tiny builders live inside.
A termite mound is made of mud.
log: A log is made of wood.
A frog can sit on a log.
rock: Frogs and turtles rest on rocks.
lotus: A lotus. It grows in water.
river: A river runs to the sea.
palm: A sugar palm. It is very tall.
Palm leaves sway in the wind.
cloud: A cloud. The Sky King lives far up.
A cloud is soft and white.
small-cloud: A little cloud can carry a buffalo!
reeds: Reeds. Reeds are tall grasses that grow by water.
grass: Grass. Grass is a green plant that covers the ground.
flowers: Flowers. Flowers are the colourful part of a plant.
ferns: Ferns. A fern is a plant with feathery leaves.
plants: Plants. They grow by the river.
A banana plant has big leaves.
knoll: A knoll. It is a small hill.
A knoll is soft and round.
mound: A mound. It is a heap of earth.
A mound is higher than the ground.

notes.touch lines: tools/voice.py builds a touch line's say from its raw text, so touch lines cannot carry helper spellings; the tap lines that name Pu Nyeu, Nya Nyeu or Khun Borom are read with plain spellings unless voice.py applies this map.
notes.who speaks: 1.5 and 8.3: both grandparents speak together, voice `both`; 5.2 round then square; 7.3 people then `child` (no door voice in the dark); 7.5: the narrator reads the whole line, quoted question included, because nobody asked it.
notes.the names' sound: Eddie, 2026-11-14, by ear (sample 2 of renders/gourd/names/names-1-to-4.m4a): ປູ່ເຍີ is said "Poo Nyer" and ຫຍ່າເຍີ "Nya Nyer". The voice model reads "Nyuh" and "Nyah" as "nigh-uh"; "Ñer" and "Ñah" give the right sounds. The printed English stays "Pu Nyeu" and "Nya Nyeu".
